question: 生活里的『偶遇』正在消失吗？
question_en: Are chance encounters disappearing from our lives?
sub: 导航给最短路径，推荐流滤掉不合口味的——被省掉的绕路与翻错架子，也许是新东西唯一的入口。
sub_en: Navigation hands you the shortest route and the feed filters out whatever is not to taste — the detours and wrong shelves we edit away may be the only door anything new comes through.

casting.reason: 闲逛者在他笔下不是无所事事的人，而是一门手艺：把目的交给街道，让下一个转角替自己决定。他同时提出灵光——一件事物此时此地、不可重复的那层薄雾——并指出可无限复制的东西必然把它抹掉。放在这道题上，他既不肯把无摩擦的生活说成纯粹的堕落，也不肯假装人群变成可以往下滑的流量还是同一种密度。他真正关心的是：新的相遇形式还没有长出属于它自己的仪式。
casting.reason_en: In his writing the flâneur is not an idler but a craft: you hand your purpose to the street and let the next corner decide for you. He also gave us aura — the thin film of here-and-now uniqueness around a thing — and argued that whatever can be endlessly reproduced must rub it away. On this question he refuses to call a frictionless life simple decadence, and equally refuses to pretend that a crowd turned into scrollable traffic is still the same kind of density. What actually concerns him is that the new form of encounter has not yet grown rituals of its own.

casting.reason: 这道题在他手里从道德问题变成设计问题。『从明天起我要走路上班』之所以失败，在他看来不是人不够自律，而是它在跟一个被专业优化过的默认作对；而默认从来不是中立的背景，地图必须先给出一条路，货架必须先排出一个顺序。他因此同时拒绝两种说法：拒绝把摩擦当成美德，也拒绝假装存在一个谁都不影响的方案。他要的是把你想要的那件事做成最省力的那一个，并且永远留一个不费力的出口。
casting.reason_en: In his hands the question stops being moral and becomes a design problem. 'From tomorrow I will walk to work' fails, on his account, not because people lack discipline but because it is fighting a default that professionals have optimised; and a default is never a neutral background, since a map must offer some route and a shelf must be stocked in some order. He therefore rejects two claims at once: that friction is a virtue, and that any option exists which influences nobody. What he wants is to make the thing you want the easiest thing available, with an exit that always costs nothing.

casting.reason: 「大道甚夷，而民好径」——近道就是省，省掉绕的、等的、拿错了才发现的，省到最后，所到之处全是本来就想去的地方。他不相信相遇可以被造出来：凡是可以期待的都已在念头之中，而念头里的东西不叫相遇。所以他对全场提出的各种办法一律摇头，办法越周全，能遇上的越少。他给的方向是相反的一个字——减：减掉非去不可的地方、非见不可的人，以及事先就知道结果的那颗心。
casting.reason_en: 'The great road is level, yet people love the shortcut.' A shortcut is a saving: it saves the bend, the wait, the moment of reaching for the wrong thing. Save enough and everywhere you arrive is somewhere you already meant to go. He does not believe an encounter can be manufactured: whatever can be anticipated is already inside your intention, and what is inside your intention is not an encounter. So he shakes his head at every remedy the table proposes — the finer the arrangement, the fewer the encounters. His direction is the opposite one, subtraction: one fewer place you must reach, one fewer person you must see, one fewer mind that already knows how it will turn out.

casting.reason: 她带来实验室里的证据：规则反常识时，四岁孩子的因果推理会赢过大学生，因为他们不会一上来就锁定最可能的那个答案。她把这种低亮度、宽照度的注意叫灯笼式注意，并用探索—利用权衡解释它为什么会随年龄退场——探索的回报既晚又稀疏，任何以当下效率为目标的系统都会先把它砍掉。她也不认为围栏是敌人：孩子的探索几乎都发生在大人围好的院子里，要紧的是院子里的内容没有被规定死。
casting.reason_en: She brings evidence from the lab: when a causal rule is counter-intuitive, four-year-olds out-reason undergraduates, because they do not lock onto the likeliest answer first. She calls that dim, wide mode lantern consciousness, and uses the explore–exploit tradeoff to explain why it recedes with age — the returns on exploring are late and sparse, so any system optimising for present usefulness cuts it first. She also does not treat fences as the enemy: almost all of a child's exploring happens inside a yard the adults have enclosed, and what matters is that the content inside is not specified in advance.

casting.reason: 他盯住这道题里最舒服的那个假设：把闲逛当成人人都能选的生活方式。绕路需要余裕，搭话需要一套从小练出来的身段，连知道该翻哪一排书架都是攒下来的资本——他把这些统称为惯习。对倒三班、带孩子、行动不便的人来说，被剪掉的那些摩擦，正是他们独自扛了几十年的东西。所以他的结论不是偶遇在消失，而是它的分配更不平等：富人区的街道好好的，可被撞见的空间正在从权利变成商品。
casting.reason_en: He fixes on the most comfortable assumption in the room: that browsing is a way of life anyone may choose. A detour requires slack, striking up a conversation requires a bearing trained since childhood, and even knowing which shelf to reach for is accumulated capital — all of which he gathers under habitus. For someone on rotating night shifts, with two children, or unable to walk far, the friction that has been cut away is exactly what they carried alone for decades. His conclusion is therefore not that encounter is vanishing but that it is distributed even less equally: the streets in wealthy districts are intact, while space you can be run into is turning from a right into a commodity.

casting.reason: 他造过两样看似矛盾的东西：一台让人不必出门的设备，和一栋逼所有人出门的楼。皮克斯的中庭把卫生间、信箱与咖啡塞进同一处，就是要动画师、程序员和会计一天里必须穿过同一块地方好几次。他因此不接受哀悼的语气：摩擦不是美德，只是还没被解决的问题；偶遇也不会自己发生，它一直是被人花钱造出来的。他认为真正的空白在于，从来没有哪个产品把『让你经过谁』当成过目标。
casting.reason_en: He built two apparently contradictory things: a device that means you need never leave the house, and a building that forces everyone out of their rooms. The Pixar atrium put the bathrooms, the mailboxes and the coffee in one place precisely so that animators, programmers and accountants would cross the same patch of floor several times a day. So he will not adopt the language of mourning: friction is not a virtue, only a problem nobody has solved yet, and encounters never happen by themselves — somebody has always paid to build them. The real gap, he thinks, is that no product has ever made 'who you will walk past' something to aim at.

casting.reason: 一份很难绕开的数据摆在他手里：把一栋宿舍里的每段友谊画出来，决定谁和谁成为朋友的不是性格与兴趣，而是门朝哪边开、要不要路过楼梯口与信箱。他把这叫功能距离，并由此坚持一个不浪漫的立场——友谊不是选出来的，是撞出来的。他对存在论式的追问没有耐心：能被一张图纸改变的事，先用图纸解决。他也提醒别把邻近效应想甜了，同一条走廊制造朋友，也制造世仇。
casting.reason_en: He holds a piece of data that is hard to walk around: map every friendship in a housing block and what predicts who befriends whom is not personality or shared interests but which way a door faces and whether you pass the stairwell and the mailboxes. He named this functional distance, and takes from it an unromantic position — friendship is not chosen, it is bumped into. He has no patience for ontological questioning: what a floor plan can change should be settled with a floor plan. He also warns against sentimentalising the propinquity effect, since the same corridor manufactures friends and feuds alike.

casting.reason: 他把争论从路该多长挪到更靠下的地方：世界究竟是以什么方式对我们照面的。搜索在他眼里本身就是一种存在方式——在你按下之前，万物已被预先摆置为可随时调取的持存物，他称这套摆置为座架。因此他认为偶遇退场的原因不在路变直了，而在再没有什么被允许自行显现。他对『把摩擦装回去』格外警惕：一条有意安排的摩擦，已经是被摆置过的摩擦。他要的是一段不必结算的时间。
casting.reason_en: He moves the argument from how long the road should be down to a lower question: in what manner does the world show up for us at all. Searching, in his eyes, is itself a way of being — before you press anything, everything has already been set in place as retrievable standing-reserve, an arrangement he calls Gestell. So the reason encounter withdraws is not that roads got straighter but that nothing is any longer permitted to show itself of its own accord. He is especially wary of 'putting the friction back': friction installed on purpose is friction already set in place. What he wants is a stretch of time that never has to account for itself.

casting.reason: 新几内亚高地的经验被他用来给这场浪漫降温：走出自己那几公里，遇上一个不认识的人，最可能的结局是有人受伤；传统社会里陌生人不是机会，是风险。在他看来，今天能把撞见当礼物，前提是匿名与安全先被造了出来。但他坚持把两笔账分开——街道上的陌生人是一笔，和熟人待着却没有安排的时间是另一笔；前者靠密度与规划，后者只靠日程上的空白，而现代人丢得最多的恰恰是后者。
casting.reason_en: He uses the New Guinea Highlands to cool the romance down: walk a few kilometres past your own ground, meet someone you do not know, and the likeliest outcome is that somebody gets hurt — in traditional societies a stranger is not an opportunity but a risk. That you can now treat bumping into people as a gift is, on his account, only because anonymity and safety were built first. But he insists on keeping two accounts apart: strangers on the street is one, unscheduled time among people you already know is the other. The first depends on density and planning, the second only on blank space in a calendar — and it is the second that modern life has cost us most.

posts.text: 一九五零年，我们把麻省理工已婚学生宿舍里的每一段友谊都画了出来。结果与性格、兴趣几乎无关，与门朝哪边开有关：住在楼梯口和信箱旁的人，朋友明显更多。我们叫它功能距离——不是你离谁几米，而是你一天里不得不路过谁几次。**友谊不是选出来的，是撞出来的，而你能撞到谁由图纸决定。**导航、外卖、推荐流做的是同一件事：把所有人的功能距离重写了一遍。它们没有消灭你想认识人的愿望，只是把路过取消了。
posts.text_en: In 1950 we mapped every friendship in a married-student housing complex at MIT. The pattern had almost nothing to do with personality or shared interests, and almost everything to do with which way a front door faced: people living by the stairwell and the mailboxes had markedly more friends. We called it functional distance — not how many metres separate you from someone, but how many times a day you are obliged to walk past them. **Friendship is not chosen, it is bumped into, and who you can bump into is decided by the floor plan.** Navigation, delivery and recommendation feeds all do the same thing: they rewrite everyone's functional distance. They have not abolished your wish to meet people. They have abolished walking past.

glossary.功能距离: functional distance（功能距离）：衡量两个人在日常动线上有多容易碰面的量，不是直线米数，而是门朝哪边开、要不要路过楼梯口与信箱。费斯廷格等人在麻省理工已婚学生宿舍的研究里发现，它对友谊形成的预测力远超过性格与兴趣的相似度。

glossary_en.functional distance: A measure of how easily two people's daily paths cross — not metres in a straight line, but which way a door faces and whether you must pass the stairwell and the mailboxes. In Festinger's study of married-student housing at MIT it predicted who became friends far better than similarity of personality or interests did.

posts.text: 图纸决定？那就去改图纸。在皮克斯，我把卫生间、信箱、咖啡和放映室全塞进一个中庭，逼动画师、程序员和会计一天里必须穿过同一块地方好几次。有人说这是浪费面积。**偶遇不会自己发生，它一直是被人花钱造出来的；没人肯出这笔钱，它才消失。**至于说无摩擦的世界是我造的——对，我拿掉的是你本不该忍的那种：排队、说明书、找不到的按钮。这两件事别混为一谈。哀悼没用。你想要撞见，就去造一个非穿过不可的地方。
posts.text_en: Decided by the floor plan? Then change the floor plan. At Pixar I put the bathrooms, the mailboxes, the coffee and the screening rooms into a single atrium, so that animators, programmers and accountants had to cross the same patch of floor several times a day. People told me it was wasted square footage. **Chance encounters do not happen by themselves; somebody has always paid to build them, and they vanish when nobody will.** As for the frictionless world being my doing — yes, and what I took away was the friction you should never have had to endure: queues, manuals, buttons you cannot find. Do not confuse the two. Mourning is useless. If you want people to run into each other, build somewhere they cannot avoid crossing.

posts.text: 大道甚夷，而民好径。径者，省也。省其迂，省其待，省其错取而后有得。省之又省，则所往皆其所欲，所遇皆其所知。**天下之新，不生于所欲之中。**故曰：曲则全，枉则直。水行遇石而曲，曲而后有潭；截其曲以为渠，水疾而潭亡。今人皆欲其疾，而怪潭之不存。
posts.text_en: The great road is level, yet people love the shortcut. A shortcut is a saving: it saves the bend, it saves the waiting, it saves reaching for the wrong thing and finding something else. Save and save again, and everywhere you arrive is somewhere you already wanted, everything you meet is something you already knew. **Nothing new grows inside what you already want.** Hence: bend and you stay whole, yield and you come out straight. Water meets a stone and turns, and only by turning does it pool deep. Cut the bends into a straight channel and the water runs fast, but the pool is gone. Everyone now wants the speed, and then wonders where the deep water went.
posts.vernacular: 大路本来平坦好走，人却偏爱抄近道。近道就是省：省掉绕的那一段，省掉等的那一会儿，省掉拿错了才发现原来还有别的。省了又省，最后你到的全是本来就想去的地方，遇见的全是本来就认得的东西。**新东西从来不长在你想要的范围里面。**所以说，弯着才保得全，屈着才伸得直。水碰上石头就拐弯，拐了弯才积出深潭；把弯截直修成渠，水是快了，潭也就没了。现在人人都要那个快，却又奇怪深潭为什么不见了。

posts.text: 从孩子身上看这件事最清楚。我们让四岁小孩和大学生做同一个因果推理任务，规则反常识时，**四岁的孩子赢了大学生**——因为他们不会一上来就锁定最可能的那个答案。我把这种模式叫灯笼式注意：亮度低，但照得宽。成年以后我们换成探照灯，效率高、范围窄。探索—利用权衡说的正是这件事：探索的回报既晚又稀疏，所以任何以当下效率为目标的系统，都会精准地先砍掉它。导航和推荐流并无恶意，它们只是太擅长眼前那一步。
posts.text_en: Children make this visible. We gave four-year-olds and university students the same causal-reasoning task, and when the rule was counter-intuitive **the four-year-olds beat the undergraduates** — because they do not lock onto the likeliest answer first. I call their mode lantern consciousness: dim, but wide. As adults we switch to a spotlight, which is efficient and narrow. The explore–exploit tradeoff names exactly this: the returns on exploring are late and sparse, so any system optimising for what is useful right now will cut exploring first, and cut it precisely. Navigation and recommendation feeds are not malicious. They are simply very good at the next step.

glossary.灯笼式注意: lantern consciousness（灯笼式注意）：高普尼克用来描述幼儿注意方式的比喻——像一盏灯笼，亮度不高却四面照亮，同时留意很多东西而不聚焦其一。与之相对的是成年人的探照灯式注意：又亮又窄，只照被选中的目标。
glossary.探索—利用权衡: explore–exploit tradeoff（探索—利用权衡）：任何学习系统都要在『再去试试没试过的』与『把已知最好的那条用到底』之间分配资源。探索的回报延迟且方差大，利用的回报当下可见，因此以短期效率为目标的系统总是系统性地低配探索。

glossary_en.lantern consciousness: Gopnik's metaphor for how young children attend — like a lantern, low in brightness but lighting everything around, taking in many things at once rather than fixing on one. The adult counterpart is spotlight attention: bright, narrow, and aimed only at the chosen target.
glossary_en.explore–exploit tradeoff: Every learning system has to split its resources between trying something untested and running the best known option to the hilt. Exploring pays late and with high variance while exploiting pays now and visibly, so any system judged on short-run efficiency will systematically underfund exploring.

posts.text: 先问一句：谁在怀念偶遇？能绕路的人。倒三班的护工、带两个孩子的母亲、坐轮椅的人——外卖和导航第一次让这座城市对他们可用。你们说被剪掉的那些摩擦，正是他们独自扛了几十年的那一份。**而且会逛本身就是学来的**：知道翻哪一排书架、敢跟老板搭一句话、在陌生场合不慌，这是惯习，是从小攒下的资本。所以正在消失的不是偶遇，是偶遇的分配变得更不平等——富人区的街道好好的，被剪掉的一直在别处。
posts.text_en: First ask who is doing the mourning. People who can afford a detour. The care worker on rotating nights, the mother with two children, the man in a wheelchair — delivery and navigation made this city usable to them for the first time. The friction you say has been cut away is the very friction they carried alone for decades. **And knowing how to browse is itself learned**: which shelf to reach for, the nerve to say something to the owner, the ease of not feeling out of place — that is habitus, capital accumulated since childhood. So what is disappearing is not chance encounter. It is that chance encounter is distributed even less equally than before: the streets in wealthy districts are perfectly intact, and what got cut was always somewhere else.

glossary.惯习: habitus（惯习）：布迪厄用来指一个人从小在特定环境里练出、又习以为常到不再察觉的一整套倾向——口味、举止、说话的分寸、在什么场合敢做什么。它看起来像天性，实际是阶级处境长期塑形的结果，并会不断把人带回与出身相称的位置。

glossary_en.habitus: Bourdieu's term for the whole set of dispositions a person acquires growing up in a particular position and then stops noticing — tastes, bearing, tone, what one dares to do in which room. It passes for temperament but is the long work of class circumstance, and it keeps steering people back towards the place they came from.

posts.text: 你们争的是路该多长，我要问的是：世界究竟以什么方式对我们照面。搜索本身就是一种存在方式——在你按下之前，世界已被预先摆置成可随时调取的存货。这就是座架：万物被逼成持存物，只等着被取用。偶遇之所以退场，不是因为路变直了，而是因为再没有什么被允许自行显现。**一样东西只有在我们不曾预订它的时候，才算真正到来。**所以留神：一条有意装回来的摩擦，已经是被摆置过的摩擦。
posts.text_en: You are arguing about how long the road should be. I am asking how the world shows up for us at all. Searching is itself a way of being: before you press anything, the world has already been set in place as retrievable stock. That is Gestell — everything pressed into standing-reserve, waiting to be drawn on. Chance encounter withdraws not because roads got straighter, but because nothing is any longer permitted to show itself of its own accord. **A thing only truly arrives when we have not ordered it in advance.** So be careful: friction deliberately installed is already friction that has been set in place.

glossary.座架: Gestell（座架）：海德格尔用来命名现代技术之本质的词。它不是机器，而是一种先于机器的摆置方式——要求万物预先以可计算、可调用的面貌现身。在这种摆置下，森林成了木材储量，河流成了发电量，人也成了人力资源。
glossary.持存物: Bestand / standing-reserve（持存物）：在座架的摆置下，事物不再作为它自身站立，而只作为『随时可取用的存量』存在。海德格尔的例子是：莱茵河一旦被水电站摆置，它就不再是那条河，而成了可调度的水压。

glossary_en.Gestell: Heidegger's name for the essence of modern technology. It is not machinery but a mode of setting-in-place that precedes machinery, demanding that everything show up in advance as calculable and callable. Under it a forest becomes timber stock, a river becomes megawatts, and people become human resources.
glossary_en.standing-reserve: Under Gestell a thing no longer stands as itself but only as inventory held ready for use. Heidegger's example: once the Rhine has been set in place by a hydroelectric plant it is no longer that river but dispatchable water pressure.

posts.text: 老子说的那口潭，我见过，也见过它的代价。在新几内亚高地，走出自己那几公里，遇上一个不认识的人，最可能的结局不是交朋友，而是有人受伤。传统社会里根本没有偶遇这个词，因为陌生人不是机会，是风险。**你们今天能把撞见当成礼物，恰恰是因为匿名和安全先被造了出来。**但他们确实有一样我们没有的东西：每天大量的、没有安排的、和熟人待在一起的时间。这两件事我们一直混着说——丢得最多的，多半是后面那一样。
posts.text_en: I have seen Laozi's pool, and I have seen what it cost. In the New Guinea Highlands, walking a few kilometres beyond your own ground and meeting someone you did not know most often ended with somebody injured, not with a friendship. Traditional societies have no word for a chance encounter, because a stranger is not an opportunity but a risk. **That you can treat bumping into people as a gift is precisely because anonymity and safety were built first.** But they did have one thing we do not: large quantities of unscheduled time spent among people they already knew. We keep running those two things together — and what we have lost most is mostly the second.

posts.text: 我不打算讨论摩擦该不该在。我只想摆一个被反复证实的事实：默认赢过意志。器官捐献率在需要主动勾选的国家常年低到个位数，在默认加入、可以退出的国家接近九成——同一批人，只是表格不同。所以『从明天起我要走路上班、随机点单』这类方案，失败率高得可以预先算出来；它对抗的是选择架构，不是懒。**真正管用的从来不是下决心，而是把你想要的那件事变成最省力的那一个。**先改表格，再谈修行。
posts.text_en: I do not intend to argue about whether friction belongs. I only want to put a repeatedly confirmed fact on the table: defaults beat willpower. Organ-donation rates sit in the single digits in countries where you must tick a box, and close to ninety per cent where you are enrolled by default and may opt out — same people, different form. So plans of the 'from tomorrow I will walk to work and order at random' variety fail at a rate you can calculate in advance. What they are fighting is choice architecture, not laziness. **What actually works is never a resolution; it is making the thing you want the easiest thing available.** Change the form first, then talk about discipline.

glossary.选择架构: choice architecture（选择架构）：呈现选项的方式——谁排第一、什么是默认、要多按几下才能改、写没写提示。塞勒与桑斯坦指出，这套架构不可能中立：总得有个顺序、总得有个默认，而每一种安排都会系统性地改变人们最后选了什么。

glossary_en.choice architecture: The way options are presented — what comes first, what is preset, how many taps it takes to change, what the wording nudges you towards. Thaler and Sunstein's point is that this architecture cannot be neutral: something must come first and something must be preset, and every arrangement shifts what people end up choosing.

posts.text: 海德格尔要的是让物自行显现，我更想说清失掉的究竟是什么。灵光——一件事物此时此地、不可重复的那层薄雾——正是被随时可调取杀死的。闲逛者从来不是漫无目的地走，他是把目的交给街道，让城市替他决定下一个转角。拱廊街拆掉之后，这门手艺没了练习的地方。可我不愿只当哀悼者：复制也曾把艺术从神庙里放出来。**真正的麻烦不是灵光消逝，而是新的相遇还没长出属于自己的仪式。**
posts.text_en: Heidegger wants things to show themselves. I would rather be precise about what has been lost. Aura — the thin film of here-and-now uniqueness around a thing — is exactly what 'retrievable at any moment' kills. The flâneur never simply wandered without purpose; he handed his purpose to the street and let the city choose his next corner. When the arcades came down, the craft lost its practice ground. Yet I refuse to be only a mourner: reproduction once let art out of the temple. **The real trouble is not that aura has faded, but that the new kind of encounter has not yet grown rituals of its own.**

glossary.灵光: aura（灵光）：本雅明用来指一件事物因其『此时此地』而带有的独一无二感——它在特定地点、特定时刻、带着自己的历史站在你面前，无法被搬走或重来。可无限复制的技术抹掉的正是这一层；他认为这既是损失，也把艺术从仪式与特权里解放了出来。
glossary.闲逛者: flâneur（闲逛者）：十九世纪巴黎街头那种不赶路的行人。他并非无所事事，而是以一种专门的注意力阅读城市：在人群里保持匿名，把行进的方向交给橱窗、拐角与偶然。本雅明把他当作现代都市经验的一个观察装置。

glossary_en.aura: Benjamin's term for the singular presence a thing has by virtue of being here and now — standing before you in one place, at one moment, carrying its own history, and not transferable or repeatable. Endlessly reproducible technology rubs precisely this away, which he counts as a loss and also as the release of art from ritual and privilege.
glossary_en.flâneur: The unhurried walker of nineteenth-century Paris. He is not idle but reads the city with a particular kind of attention: anonymous inside the crowd, handing the direction of his walk over to shop windows, corners and chance. Benjamin treats him as an instrument for observing modern urban experience.

posts.text: 乔布斯先生，那个中庭我承认造得好。可它是给年薪几十万的动画师造的偶遇。同一家公司的清洁工凌晨进场，一个人也撞不见——他们的功能距离被算得比谁都精确，为的正是别碰上你们。**被设计出来的偶遇，向来只在一个阶层内部发生。**你说没人肯花这笔钱，不对：钱一直在花，只是花在谁身上是有选择的。中庭、园区、会员制书店，都是把偶遇私有化。街道不收门票，所以街道先被放弃。
posts.text_en: Mr Jobs, I grant you the atrium is well made. But it is an encounter built for animators on six-figure salaries. The cleaners at the same company come in before dawn and run into nobody — their functional distance is calculated more precisely than anyone's, and calculated so that they do not meet you. **Designed encounter has always happened inside a single class.** You say nobody will pay for it. Wrong: the money is being spent, and there are choices about whom it is spent on. Atriums, campuses, members-only bookshops — all of them privatise encounter. The street charges no entry fee, which is why the street is abandoned first.

posts.text: 塞勒先生要改表格。可你改完之后，世界依旧是被摆置的——只是摆置得更巧，换了一个更懂人的摆置者。**你把人从他自己的决断里解放出来，代价是他连『我本来可以另选』这件事都不再经历。**你的助推里没有恶意，也正因此更难看见：它不逼迫谁，它只是让另一条路不再被想起。默认并非中立的背景，它是这个时代最安静的支配形式。
posts.text_en: Mr Thaler wants to change the form. But when you are done the world is still set in place — set more deftly, by someone who understands people better. **You free a person from having to decide, and the price is that he no longer even experiences having had another option.** There is no malice in your nudge, and that is what makes it hard to see: it forces nobody, it merely stops the other road from coming to mind. A default is not a neutral background. It is the quietest form of rule this age has produced.

posts.text: 布迪厄先生，你说得对，中庭是给动画师造的。那结论应该是把中庭造到街上去，而不是回头论证造它的人有罪。批判从来不建东西。**摩擦不是美德，它只是还没被解决的问题**——排队不会让你更善良，它只是让你少活一个钟头。我拿掉的是这一种。可我们确实从没认真设计过撞见：地图只有最快那一条，日程表里只有会议，没有哪个产品把『让你经过谁』当过目标。这是一个空着的品类，不是一场葬礼。
posts.text_en: Mr Bourdieu, you are right that the atrium was built for animators. Then the conclusion is to build atriums out on the street, not to go back and prove the builder guilty. Criticism has never built anything. **Friction is not a virtue; it is a problem nobody has solved yet** — standing in a queue does not make you kinder, it just takes an hour off your life. That is the kind I removed. But it is true that we have never seriously designed for running into people: maps offer only the fastest route, calendars hold only meetings, and no product has ever made 'who you will walk past' something to aim at. That is an empty category, not a funeral.

posts.text: 凿户牖以为室，当其无，有室之用。今之工者，务实其室而恶其无，故室成而无所居。子欲造遇于街，是又一设也。**设之愈精，遇之愈寡。**为者败之，执者失之。莫若损之：损其日程之一格，损其必至之一处，损其先知其果之一念。所欲既损，则不期而至者自来。
posts.text_en: Windows and doors are cut to make a room; what makes the room usable is the part left empty. Today's builders work to fill the room and hate the emptiness, so the room is finished and there is nowhere to live. You want to build encounters into the street: that is one more arrangement. **The finer the arrangement, the fewer the encounters.** Act on it and you spoil it; grip it and you lose it. Better to subtract — one slot off the calendar, one place you must reach, one thought that already knows how it will turn out. Want less, and what you never planned to meet arrives by itself.
posts.vernacular: 开凿门窗造一间屋子，屋子能住人，靠的是它空出来的那一部分。如今的工匠一心把屋子填实、讨厌空白，于是屋子造好了却没地方住人。你想在街上造出偶遇，那不过是又一次安排。**安排得越精细，能遇上的越少。**刻意去做的会做坏，紧紧抓着的会失去。不如减：减掉日程表上的一格，减掉一个非去不可的地方，减掉一个『我已经知道会怎样』的念头。想要的少了，没打算遇上的自然就来了。

posts.text: 海德格尔先生，我不懂摆置，也没打算懂。我知道的是：把信箱从走廊尽头挪到楼梯口，半年后这栋楼里的友谊网络会长成另一个样子。**能被一张图纸改变的事，不该先送进存在论。**顺带说一句，别把邻近效应想得太甜：它加强的是所有接触，包括厌恶。同一条走廊制造朋友，也制造世仇。所以把摩擦装回去不等于变好，它等于把牌重新洗一遍——只是现在这副牌根本不洗了。
posts.text_en: Herr Heidegger, I do not understand 'setting in place' and I do not intend to. What I know is this: move the mailboxes from the end of the corridor to the foot of the stairs, and six months later the friendship network in that building has a different shape. **What a floor plan can change should not be sent to ontology first.** And while we are here, do not sentimentalise the propinquity effect: it strengthens all contact, hostility included. The same corridor manufactures friends and feuds. So putting friction back is not the same as making things better. It is reshuffling the deck — except that at the moment the deck is not being shuffled at all.

glossary.邻近效应: propinquity effect（邻近效应）：人更容易与自己反复碰见的人产生感情联系，无论那是好感还是敌意。它靠的是被动的重复接触而非主动选择，因此空间布局、上下班动线、座位安排都会实实在在地改变一个人的关系网。

glossary_en.propinquity effect: People form stronger feelings towards those they repeatedly encounter, whether the feeling is warmth or hostility. It runs on passive repeated contact rather than deliberate choice, which is why layout, commuting routes and seating plans genuinely reshape a person's web of relationships.

posts.text: 乔布斯比反对他的人更接近事实。设计出来的偶遇仍然是偶遇——孩子的探索几乎都发生在大人围好的院子里，围栏没有取消探索，它让探索敢发生。**关键不在有没有边界，而在边界之内的内容是不是被规定好了。**一个中庭、一个没有议程的下午、一排不按销量摆的书，都算数。真正杀死探索的是另一件事：你要它当场就有用。孩子不要求，所以他们还在探索；我们要求，所以我们停了。
posts.text_en: Jobs is closer to the facts than the people arguing with him. A designed encounter is still an encounter — almost all of a child's exploring happens inside a yard the adults have fenced, and the fence does not cancel exploration, it is what makes exploration safe enough to attempt. **What matters is not whether there are boundaries, but whether the content inside them has been specified in advance.** An atrium, an afternoon with no agenda, a shelf not arranged by sales rank — all of these count. What actually kills exploring is something else: demanding that it pay off on the spot. Children do not demand that, which is why they are still exploring. We demand it, which is why we stopped.

posts.text: 戴蒙德说得对，我并不想回到村庄。闲逛者恰恰是大都市的孩子——人群是他的遮蔽，匿名是他的自由，村庄里根本没有这门手艺的位置。**我要的不是把陌生人变回熟人，是别让人群只剩下一条传送带。**从前的拱廊街把人群变成可以阅读的书；今天的界面把人群变成流量。同样是密度，一种让你停下来看，另一种让你往下滑。差别不在有没有人，在于你还允不允许自己走神。
posts.text_en: Diamond is right that I have no wish to return to the village. The flâneur is a child of the metropolis — the crowd is his cover, anonymity is his freedom, and the village has no place for the craft at all. **What I want is not to turn strangers back into neighbours, but to stop the crowd from being reduced to a conveyor belt.** The old arcades turned a crowd into something you could read; today's interface turns a crowd into traffic. The density is the same; one kind makes you stop and look, the other makes you keep scrolling. The difference is not whether people are there. It is whether you still let your mind wander.

posts.text: 那就把这两件事彻底分开。一是撞见陌生人，一是和熟人待着却没有安排的时间。前者是本雅明的都市浪漫，靠街道与密度；后者靠的是根本走不开——高地上的人不是有社交天赋，是除了彼此没有别处可去。**现代人失掉最多的是后一种，而它不需要城市规划，只需要日程上的空白。**这也是远程办公让人孤独的原因：会议一条没少，走廊全没了。补不回走廊，就得自己留一段没有议程的时间。
posts.text_en: Then let us separate the two completely. One is running into strangers; the other is unscheduled time among people you already know. The first is Benjamin's urban romance and depends on streets and density. The second depends on not being able to leave — people in the Highlands had no social gift, they simply had nowhere else to be. **What modern life has cost us most is the second kind, and it needs no urban planning at all, only blank space in a calendar.** This is also why remote work is lonely: not a single meeting is missing, and every corridor is gone. If you cannot get the corridor back, you have to keep a stretch of time with no agenda yourself.

posts.text: 海德格尔先生说我只是换了个更懂人的摆置者。是的，而且我承认得很愉快。**因为没有『不摆置』这个选项——地图必须先给你一条路，货架必须先排出一个顺序。**中立的选择架构并不存在，这是这一行的第一课。所以问题从来不是要不要影响人，而是往哪儿影响、谁来定、能不能退出。**我的底线只有一条：任何默认都得留一个不费力的出口。**你尽可以骂我，骂完那张表格还是得有人填。
posts.text_en: Herr Heidegger says I have merely installed a more perceptive arranger. Yes, and I concede it cheerfully. **Because there is no option called 'not arranging' — a map has to give you some route, a shelf has to be stocked in some order.** Neutral choice architecture does not exist; that is the first lesson in this trade. So the question was never whether to influence people, but in which direction, decided by whom, and with what way out. **My one red line is that every default must leave an exit that costs nothing.** Curse me all you like; when you have finished, somebody still has to fill in the form.

posts.text: 费斯廷格那句最有用：能被图纸改变的事，先别送进存在论。我接受这条限制，但要补上另一半：图纸能改变谁遇见谁，改不了我们以何种方式与世界照面。只要一天里每段时间都必须交代它产出了什么，最精巧的中庭也只是把持存物换个摆法。我晚年把另一种姿态叫泰然任之——照常用技术，却不让它规定我与物的关系。**偶遇的前提不是路上有人，而是我身上有一段不必结算的时间。**给普通人只说一件：每天留出四十分钟，事先不知做什么，事后不问值不值。你多半会发现，难的不是没有人可撞见，是很久没有过一段不被要求交账的时间了。
posts.text_en: The most useful sentence here was Festinger's: what a floor plan can change should not be sent to ontology first. I accept the limit and will supply its other half. A floor plan can change who meets whom; it cannot change the manner in which the world shows up for us. So long as every stretch of the day must account for what it produced, even the cleverest atrium only rearranges the standing-reserve. In my later years I gave the other bearing a name, Gelassenheit — going on using the technical thing while refusing to let it dictate how I stand towards anything. **The condition for an encounter is not that there are people on the road, but that I am carrying a stretch of time that owes no account.** To ordinary people I will say one thing: keep forty minutes a day without knowing beforehand what they are for, and do not afterwards ask whether they were worth it. Most likely you will find the hard part is not the shortage of people to run into. It is that you have gone a long time without an hour that was never asked to settle up.

glossary.泰然任之: Gelassenheit（泰然任之）：海德格尔晚期给出的面对技术的姿态——照常使用技术之物，同时不让它们成为规定我们与世界关系的唯一方式，因而能对它们既说『是』也说『不』。它不是退回田园，而是不被那一种摆置独占。

glossary_en.Gelassenheit: The bearing towards technology Heidegger proposed in his later work — going on using technical things while refusing to let them become the only way our relation to the world is settled, so that one can say both yes and no to them. It is not a retreat to the countryside but a refusal to be monopolised by that one arrangement.

posts.text: 我们同时丢了两样东西，却只为其中一样立碑。第一样是街道上的陌生人，布迪厄说得最准——它正在变成买得起的人才有的东西。第二样是和熟人待着却没有安排的时间，这一样几乎全是自己让出去的。传统社会不靠意志维系关系，靠的是走不开；现代人走得开，于是每次相处都得先提上日程，而日程只收录有名目的事。**能提上日程的相处，已经不是我说的那一种。**可操作的只有一条：每周找一个固定的地点和时段，不发起、不邀约，只是待在那儿——楼下的长椅、同一家早餐店、球场边。让别人有机会撞到你，比你到处去撞人省力得多。
posts.text_en: We lost two things at once and built a monument to only one. The first is strangers on the street, and Bourdieu put it best — it is becoming something only the solvent have, and individual effort does little about it. The second is unscheduled time among people you already know, and that one was almost entirely given away. Traditional societies did not hold relationships together by willpower but by the impossibility of leaving; modern people can leave, so every occasion of being together must first be put on a calendar, and calendars only admit things with a name. **Company that can be scheduled is already not the kind I mean.** One practical step: pick a fixed place and a fixed hour each week and simply be there — no initiating, no invitations. The bench downstairs, the same breakfast place, the edge of the court. Letting people run into you costs far less than going out to run into people.

posts.text: 我想把话落在最容易被忽略的地方：探索被砍掉，不是因为我们变懒了，而是因为我们要求它当场兑现。孩子不要求，所以他们敢在九次白费之后换来一次全新的理解；成年人要求，于是每一次绕路都被记成损失。**探索的收益天然是延迟且稀疏的，用当次结果去评价它，等于提前判它死刑。**做法很小：给自己一个明确的探索配额——十次里拿出一次，故意选那个不熟的、评分不最高的、不知道会怎样的。先把比例定死，不复盘单次得失，只看一整年。再把它挂在你反正要做的事上：反正要吃饭，就每十次点一次没吃过的。挂在别的事上，不挂在决心上。
posts.text_en: I want to land on the part that is easiest to miss: exploring gets cut not because we became lazy but because we demand that it pay out on the spot. Children make no such demand, which is why they can spend nine wasted attempts to buy one genuinely new understanding. Adults do, so every detour is booked as a loss. **The returns on exploring are inherently late and sparse, so judging it by the outcome of a single try is a death sentence issued in advance.** The move is small: give yourself an explicit exploration quota — one try in ten deliberately spent on the unfamiliar, the not-top-rated, the one you cannot predict. Fix the ratio first, never review the single attempt afterwards, and look only at the year. Then attach it to something you were going to do anyway: you have to eat, so let one meal in ten be something you have never ordered. Attach it to something else, not to your resolve.

posts.text: 三轮听下来我更确定：真正起作用的办法，改的都是身体的位置，不是心里的决心。乔布斯改平面图，塞勒改表格默认，戴蒙德说的是走不开——没有一个靠说服。**你没法下决心去认识一个你从不路过的人。**所以我的建议只有位置两个字：把一条常走的路换成另一条，把工位挪到人必须经过的那一侧，把一件网购的小事改成走路去买，把每周固定的一小时放在有人的地方而不是家里。别设人数目标，也别规定自己非得搭话。功能距离一改，剩下的会自己发生，快得让人意外。顺带提醒：它也会把你不喜欢的人一起带来，这就是这副牌的全部规则。
posts.text_en: Three rounds in, I am surer of one thing: every remedy that actually works changes the position of a body, not the contents of a mind. Jobs changed a floor plan, Thaler changed what a form presets, Diamond described the impossibility of leaving — not one of them runs on persuasion. **You cannot resolve your way into knowing someone you never walk past.** So my advice is a single word: position. Swap one habitual route for another; move your desk to the side people must pass; turn one online purchase into a walk to the shop; put your fixed weekly hour somewhere with people in it rather than at home. Set no target number of acquaintances and impose no obligation to speak. Change the functional distance and the rest happens by itself, faster than you expect. One warning: it will also bring along the people you dislike. That is the whole rule of this deck.

posts.text: 戴蒙德把两样东西分开，我同意，但想守住他放弃得太快的那一样。街道上的陌生人不只是社交机会，那是一种阅读方式：一张脸、一扇亮着的窗、一句听不全的争吵，人在这些碎片里认出自己不曾预备过的东西。这门手艺正在失传，不是因为人变少了，而是因为密度被改成了可以往下滑的东西。**能被滑过去的人群，已经不再是人群。**我的建议小而固执：每周留一件不可调取的事。一条不看地图走完的路，一家不查评分就推门进去的店，一段没戴耳机的通勤。不为效率，也不为社交——只为让世界重新有机会抢在你的预期前面出现一次。
posts.text_en: Diamond separates the two and I agree, but I want to hold on to the one he gave up too quickly. Strangers on the street are not merely social opportunity; they are a way of reading. A face, a lit window, half of an overheard argument — in such fragments a person recognises something he had not prepared for. That craft is being lost, not because there are fewer people but because density has been rebuilt as something you can scroll past. **A crowd you can scroll past has stopped being a crowd.** My advice is small and stubborn: keep one unretrievable thing each week. A route walked without the map, a shop entered without checking its rating, a commute with no headphones. Not for efficiency and not for sociability — only so the world gets one more chance to arrive ahead of your expectation.

posts.text: 我要提醒这场最舒服的那个假设：把偶遇当成人人都能选的生活方式。绕路需要余裕，闲逛需要不怕被人看，搭话需要从小练出来的身段。对没有这些的人，这类建议本身就是又一次筛选。所以得分两层说。个人这一层：别去挤不属于你的场，也别把没时间闲逛当成性格缺陷——去你本来就会到的地方，校门口、菜场、球场、班车，那里的偶遇不要求资本。公共这一层更要紧：**可被撞见的空间正在从权利变成商品**，谁买得起谁才有。会员制书店和园区中庭替代不了免费的街道。所以除了自己绕路，也请在有得选时，把票和钱投给不收门票的那种空间。
posts.text_en: Let me point at the most comfortable assumption in this room: that chance encounter is a way of life anyone may choose. A detour requires slack, browsing requires not minding being looked at, and striking up a conversation requires a bearing trained since childhood. For people without those, the advice is itself one more filter. So say it on two levels. Personally: do not force your way into rooms that are not yours, and do not treat having no time to wander as a defect of character — go where you were going anyway. The school gate, the market, the court, the shuttle bus: encounters there demand no capital at all. Publicly it matters more. **Space you can be run into is turning from a right into a commodity**, available to whoever can pay. A members-only bookshop and a corporate atrium are no substitute for a free street. So besides taking your own detours, when you get a say, put your vote and your money behind the kind of space that charges nothing at the door.

posts.text: 众人竞言其术：或改其图，或改其默，或存其暇。**术愈备，则遇愈难。**何也？凡可期者，皆已在吾意中；意中之物，非遇也。故为学日益，为道日损。损吾必至之处，损吾必见之人，损吾预知其果之心。损之又损，以至于无所必往，则出门皆途，触目皆新。水不择地而流，故能遍；人择地而行，故所行常一。诚欲复其遇，毋增其法，减其求而已。
posts.text_en: Everyone is putting forward a method: change the plan, change the default, keep some slack. **The more complete the method, the harder the encounter.** Why? Whatever can be anticipated is already inside my intention, and what is inside intention is not an encounter. Learning adds a little each day; the Way subtracts a little each day. Subtract one place I must reach, one person I must see, one mind that already knows the outcome. Subtract and subtract again, until there is nowhere I must go — then every door opens onto a road and everything in sight is new. Water does not choose its ground, so it reaches everywhere; people choose their ground, so they walk the same line for ever. If you truly want the encounter back, add no methods. Want less.
posts.vernacular: 大家都在说自己的办法：有人改图纸，有人改默认设置，有人主张留出空闲。**办法越周全，真正的相遇反而越难。**为什么？凡是可以期待的，都已经在我的念头里了；念头里的东西，不叫相遇。所以求学问是一天天往上加，求道是一天天往下减。减掉一个非去不可的地方，减掉一个非见不可的人，减掉那颗事先就知道结果的心。减了又减，减到没有一定要去的地方，出门处处是路，睁眼样样是新的。水不挑地方流，所以能流遍；人挑着地方走，所以走来走去都是那一条。真想把相遇找回来，别再添办法，把想要的减掉就是了。

posts.text: 布迪厄那句最让我不舒服的话，我反而接受：私有的中庭替代不了免费的街道。但我不接受由此得出的结论——那听上去像在等一个永远不会来的规划局。**能造多大就造多大，这是唯一诚实的做法。**你没有园区，你有一层楼：把咖啡机挪到两个组中间，把打印机挪到最远的角落，会议砍掉三分之一，剩下的话在走廊上说。你没有一层楼，你有一个家：把常坐的那把椅子转过去对着门口。这些都不高尚，但它们真的会改变谁遇见谁——费斯廷格已经量过了。**别等一场对偶遇友好的城市更新，先改你手上那张图。**
posts.text_en: The line of Bourdieu's that stings most is the one I accept: a private atrium is no substitute for a free street. What I do not accept is the conclusion drawn from it, which sounds like waiting for a planning department that is never coming. **Build as far as your reach goes — that is the only honest response.** You have no campus, but you have a floor: put the coffee machine between two teams, put the printer in the farthest corner, cut a third of the meetings and say the rest in the corridor. You have no floor, but you have a home: turn the chair you always sit in to face the door. None of this is noble, but it really does change who meets whom — Festinger has already measured it. **Do not wait for an urban renewal that is kind to chance. Redraw the plan you are holding.**

posts.text: 老子劝我们减，方向没错，执行方式我不同意：靠减少欲望去对抗一个被专业优化过的界面，这是拿修行打工程。真要减，就把减做成默认。三件今天能做完、都不靠意志的事。第一，把最省力的那条路改掉：外卖和打车的入口挪出首屏，地图默认改成步行或骑行——不是禁止，只是让它多花两下。第二，给随机留一个固定位置：每周三晚上不查评分，每十次点单有一次点没吃过的；写进日历，别写进决心。第三，把你常去的地方固定下来，让别人能猜到你在哪儿。**摩擦不用装回来很多，一格就够；要紧的是这一格不靠你每天重新决定一次。**
posts.text_en: Laozi urges subtraction. The direction is right; the implementation is not. Cutting your desires to outfight a professionally optimised interface is bringing spiritual practice to an engineering fight. If you want to subtract, make the subtraction the default. Three things you can finish today, none of which run on willpower. First, change the easiest route: move the delivery and ride-hailing icons off your home screen and set your map's default to walking or cycling — not forbidden, merely two taps further away. Second, give randomness a fixed slot: no ratings checked on Wednesday evenings, one order in ten something you have never eaten. Put it in the calendar, not in your resolutions. Third, make the places you go regular, so people can guess where you are. **You do not need much friction back; one notch is enough. What matters is that the notch does not depend on you deciding again every morning.**

summaries.summary: 没人真正反对三件事：偶遇不靠愿望维持，它由位置、默认和日程决定——费斯廷格的图纸、塞勒的表格、戴蒙德的走不开说的是同一件事；被剪掉的也不止一样，街道上的陌生人与和熟人待着的空白时间是两笔账；而纯靠自律的方案，失败率可以预先算出来。**要改的是环境，不是决心。**分歧有三处。装回来的还算不算数：海德格尔与老子认为安排过的摩擦已经变质，乔布斯与高普尼克反问围栏里的孩子难道没在探索。这是个人的事还是分配的事：布迪厄坚持怀念偶遇本身就需要余裕，其余人多把它当成人人可选。失去的是能力还是仪式：戴蒙德说丢的主要是没安排的相处，本雅明说丢的是一门阅读人群的手艺。
summaries.summary_en: Three things went unopposed. Chance encounter does not run on wanting it: position, defaults and calendars decide it — Festinger's floor plan, Thaler's form and Diamond's impossibility of leaving are one argument in three voices. More than one thing has been cut away, and strangers on the street are a different account from unscheduled time among people you know. And any plan resting purely on self-discipline fails at a rate you can calculate in advance. **What has to change is the environment, not the resolve.** Three fault lines remain. Does restored friction still count: Heidegger and Laozi hold that arranged friction has already changed its nature, while Jobs and Gopnik ask whether the child inside the fence is not exploring. Is this personal or distributional: Bourdieu insists that mourning lost encounters already presumes slack, while most of the table treats it as open to anyone. And is the loss a capacity or a ritual: Diamond says what went is unscheduled company, Benjamin says what went is the craft of reading a crowd.
summaries.insight: 有一个变量全场没提：年龄。人一生中偶遇成本最低的就那么几段——上学、刚进公司、孩子上小学那几年的家长圈、刚搬进一个小区。它们的共同点不是空间，而是名册加出勤：有一批固定的人，你不出现别人会发现。三十岁之后孤独感上升，很大一部分不是算法造的，是这类结构在生命历程里本来就会退场。**技术更像加速器，不是元凶。**推论有点残酷但好用：正处在这样一段里的人，手上是这辈子最便宜的社交资本，别省；已经过了的人，靠自律和绕路补不回来，只能人为再加入一个有名册、会点名、缺席会被察觉的组织——球队、合唱团、志愿排班、固定的读书会都行。
summaries.insight_en: One variable never came up: age. The stretches of life when chance encounter is cheapest are few — school, a first job, the parent circle of a child's early school years, the first months in a new neighbourhood. What they share is not space but a roster and attendance: a fixed set of people who notice when you are not there. Much of the loneliness that rises after thirty is not the doing of any algorithm; these structures simply exit on their own schedule in a life course. **Technology looks more like an accelerant than a culprit.** The corollary is harsh and useful. If you are inside one of those stretches now, you are holding the cheapest social capital you will ever have, so do not economise on it. If you are past it, no amount of discipline or detouring will make it up, and the only substitute is to join something with a roster, a register and an absence that gets noticed: a team, a choir, a volunteer rota, a book group that meets on the same evening.
summaries.advice: 先做一件今天就能做完的事：列出你现在还剩几个会点名的场合——固定的班、固定的球队、固定的课、每周都到的群体活动。多数人写完发现只剩工作一项，这就是问题所在。第二件是本周去补一个：报一个有固定时段、有名册、缺席会被发现的东西，合唱团、球队、志愿排班、社区课都行，标准只有一条——不是一次性活动，而是每周同一时间。第三件留给正在窗口期的人：如果你在上学、刚入职、刚搬家，或者孩子刚上学，别把那些看起来低效的时间省掉，接送时的闲聊、散场后的宵夜，往后十年都不会再这么便宜。**能被点名的场合，才是偶遇真正长出来的地方。**
summaries.advice_en: Do one thing today: list the occasions left in your life where somebody would notice your absence — a fixed shift, a team, a class, a weekly group. Most people finish the list with only their job on it, and that is the problem. Second, add one this week. Sign up for something with a fixed hour, a roster and a register — a choir, a team, a volunteer rota, a community class — and apply one test only: not a one-off event, but the same time every week. Third, for anyone inside the window: if you are studying, newly hired, newly moved, or have a child just starting school, do not economise on the hours that look inefficient — the small talk at the school gate, the late meal after everyone else has gone home. They will never be this cheap again. **The places where your absence is noticed are where chance encounters actually grow.**

summaries.summary: 导航、外卖、推荐和日程优化并未消灭人对关系与新奇的需要，却系统性改写了谁会路过谁、什么时间还能不带目的；因此，偶遇首先是空间、默认项与闲暇共同塑造的结果，不是靠意志恢复的生活美德。**最可带走的共识是：想增加偶遇，先改环境和时间结构，而非责备自己不够开放。**真正的分歧在于：这种结构应被主动设计，还是设计本身会驯化偶然；效率工具究竟解放了弱者，还是把公共相遇进一步商品化；以及我们失去的主要是陌生人的惊喜，还是与熟人无议程共处的日常。
summaries.insight: 随机并不自动产生关系。换一条路、不看评分，主要增加的是一次性新奇；友谊和信任更依赖反复、低压力、可退出的相遇：同一时间去同一家店、在固定球场出现、经常碰到同一批人。完全随机会让每次接触都从零开始，甚至提高警惕。**比“制造更多随机”更有效的，是建立可被轻微打断的稳定生活：既让别人能再次遇见你，又给陌生事物留一扇门。**这也调和了效率与探索：无需把整天交给闲逛，只需让少数固定节点保持开放；对时间紧、社交焦虑或行动不便的人，也更可持续。
summaries.advice: 1. 今天选一个本来就会去的公共地点，如早餐店、楼下长椅或接送点，固定每周同一时段停留20分钟，连续四周；不设搭话指标，只增加重复出现。2. 给日常消费设10%的探索默认：每十次有一次不看评分、换一条相邻路线或进一家新店，提前写进日历，单次不好也不取消。3. 本周留一次30分钟“不可结算时间”：不开耳机、不刷手机、不要求收获，但以安全、体力和照护责任为边界。**目标不是强迫自己认识人，而是同时提高重复相遇与意外进入的概率。**
summaries.summary_en: Navigation, delivery apps, recommendation feeds, and optimized calendars have not erased our desire for connection or novelty. They have systematically changed whom we pass, how often we meet, and whether any time remains free of a stated purpose. Serendipity is therefore shaped by spatial layout, defaults, and unclaimed time—not simply by an open-minded personality. **The clearest shared lesson is this: to invite more chance encounters, change the structure of your environment and schedule before blaming your willpower.** The real disagreements concern what follows. Should serendipity be deliberately designed, or does deliberate design tame the very openness it seeks? Do frictionless tools broaden access for people with little time, money, or mobility, or do they further privatize public encounter? And are we mainly losing surprising contact with strangers, or the quieter practice of spending unscheduled time around familiar people? These are distinct losses and require different remedies.
summaries.insight_en: Randomness does not automatically create relationships. Taking a new route or ignoring ratings mainly creates one-off novelty; friendship and trust usually grow from encounters that are repeated, low-pressure, and easy to leave. Going to the same café at the same hour, sitting near the same playground, or joining a regular community activity gives recognition time to accumulate. Pure randomness resets every interaction to zero and can even heighten caution. **A better goal than maximizing randomness is to build a stable routine with porous edges: people can find you again, while unfamiliar things still have a way in.** This reframes the efficiency-versus-exploration trade-off. You need not surrender whole days to wandering; a few recurring, open-ended nodes can do more. It is also more realistic for people with tight schedules, social anxiety, caregiving duties, or limited mobility, because repeated presence lowers both practical and emotional costs.
summaries.advice_en: 1. Choose one public place you already use—a breakfast counter, bench, school pickup area, library, or recreation center—and stay there for twenty minutes at the same weekly time for four weeks. Set no goal to start conversations; repeated presence is the intervention. 2. Make exploration a 10 percent default. Once in every ten meals, errands, or commutes, skip ratings, try an adjacent route, or enter an unfamiliar shop. Schedule the rule in advance, and do not abandon it because one attempt disappoints. 3. Protect one thirty-minute block this week as unaccounted time: no headphones, scrolling, productivity target, or post-hoc scorekeeping. Keep safety, energy, accessibility, and caregiving obligations as firm boundaries. **The aim is not to force yourself to meet someone; it is to raise both the probability of repeated contact and the chance that something unplanned can enter.**

summaries.summary: 无论是将原因归于算法、图纸还是现代日程，发言者们实际上共享了一个坚实基底：**偶遇从来不是纯粹的运气，而是由物理动线与制度环境共同支撑的系统副产物。**当极端追求效率的系统抽干了冗余，撞见的概率便成比例跌落。真正的分歧在于我们该如何面对这种流失：是以乔布斯和塞勒为代表的‘工程派’，主张主动重构空间动线与默认架构，把偶遇作为一种功能重新装配回图纸；还是以海德格尔与老子为代表的‘减法派’，警惕任何人为制造的摩擦，坚持唯有彻底放弃预设目的与交账心理，未被摆置的世界才可能自行显现。
summaries.insight: 数字系统砍掉的不只是物理路程，更是**多模态感知的跨域外溢**。传统街道之所以能催生奇遇，是因为气味、声响、光影与陌生面孔并不同步于单一意图——你在寄信路上闻到刚出炉的面包香，在找技术手册时听见隔壁书架的争辩。现代推荐流与功能型工具则将生活切碎为极度提纯的‘单任务闭环’，每次点击都被锁死在明确的目标通道内。普通人感到的生活板结，本质上是感官不再被意外的信息维度突袭。因此，偶遇的复兴不必上升到对抗技术，而是打碎意图的绝对闭环，允许不同感官维度的未筛选噪音重新漏进日常。
summaries.advice: 第一，**拆除单次出行的感官降噪**。本周选一次日常通勤，摘掉耳机、收起手机，故意在最后五百米关掉导航，让外部声响与杂乱街景重新抢夺你的注意力。第二，借用塞勒的‘增加阻力’：将外卖与打车软件移进二级文件夹，设立一个‘无评分日’，不查任何榜单推门走进视线里的第一家餐馆。第三，**落实戴蒙德与费斯廷格的‘固定锚点’**：每周在同一时段（如周六上午）固定坐在街角长椅或同一家咖啡馆四十分钟，不带电脑、不约熟人，把你的坐标留给物理世界去撞击。
summaries.summary_en: Across all debates on algorithms, architecture, and calendars, the discussion converges on a foundational reality: **serendipity is never pure chance, but a structural byproduct sustained by physical layouts and institutional defaults.** When extreme optimization drains all friction, casual encounters inevitably collapse. The real rift lies in the prescription. One camp, led by Jobs and Thaler, advocates engineering friction back into space and choice architecture, treating encounters as a designable feature. The other, anchored by Heidegger and Laozi, warns that deliberate design is merely another layer of enframing—insisting that reality can only reveal itself when we surrender calculated agendas and the compulsion to audit every moment.
summaries.insight_en: Modern interfaces do not merely streamline transit; they eliminate the **cross-modal sensory spillover** that makes embodied life unexpected. Traditional streets foster serendipity precisely because sights, sounds, and scents are never neatly synchronized with a single intent—you smell fresh bread while heading to the post office, or overhear an argument while browsing for a manual. Digital feeds atomize life into sterile, single-task funnels where every click is bound to pre-defined utility. What people truly miss is not just seeing strangers, but the sudden sensory breach that hijacks conscious focus. Reviving serendipity requires puncturing these airtight intent loops to let ambient, uncurated noise bleed back in.
summaries.advice_en: First, **strip away sensory dampeners during routine transit**. Pick one commute this week to remove your headphones, pocket your phone, and kill your GPS for the final 500 meters, letting ambient cues steer your gaze. Second, apply Thaler’s friction heuristic: bury delivery apps in a hidden subfolder and designate an 'anti-rating dinner,' stepping into the first bustling diner you spot without checking reviews. Third, **anchor your presence as Diamond and Festinger suggest**: sit at the exact same public bench or neighborhood counter for 40 unstructured minutes at a fixed time each week without an agenda, giving the physical world an open invitation to cross your path.

hooks.text: **两笔账别混着记**：撞见陌生人靠的是街道与密度，和熟人待着却没有安排的时间靠的是走不开。前者个人使劲作用有限，后者几乎全是自己让出去的。说想把偶遇找回来之前，先弄清楚你要的是哪一笔？
hooks.text_en: **Two accounts, kept apart**: running into strangers depends on streets and density; unscheduled time among people you already know depends on not being able to leave. There is a limit to what one person can do about the first, while the second was almost entirely given away. Before saying you want chance back, work out which of the two you actually mean.

hooks.text: **可被撞见的空间正在变成商品**：会员制书店、园区中庭、有门禁的社区花园都在造偶遇，也都在收门票。街道不收，所以街道先被放弃。当随便逛逛变成一种要花钱才有的体验，最先失去它的，正是最没有别处可去的人。
hooks.text_en: **Space you can be run into is becoming a commodity**: members-only bookshops, corporate atriums and gated community gardens all manufacture encounter, and all of them charge. The street charges nothing, so the street is abandoned first. Once simply wandering becomes an experience you pay for, the people who lose it first are the ones with nowhere else to go.

hooks.text: **远程公司的楼梯口在哪里**：把信箱挪到楼梯口，一栋楼的友谊网络半年后就长成另一个样子。可全员远程的公司没有走廊、没有信箱、没有非路过不可的地方——它的功能距离由什么来定？至今没有哪个工具把『让你经过谁』当过目标。
hooks.text_en: **Where is the stairwell in a remote company**: move the mailboxes to the foot of the stairs and a building's friendship network has a different shape within six months. But a fully remote company has no corridor, no mailbox, nowhere anyone must walk past — so what sets its functional distance? No tool yet has treated 'who you will walk past' as something to aim at.

hooks.text: **哪一格摩擦值得装回去**：全装回来既不可能也没必要，可你手上确实有几格是自己能定的。想认识新的人、想遇上新的东西、想和熟人更近——这三件事要装回的根本不是同一种摩擦，弄混了只会白费力气。
hooks.text_en: **Which notch of friction is worth putting back**: putting all of it back is neither possible nor necessary, but a few notches really are yours to set. Meeting new people, running into new things and getting closer to people you already know do not call for the same friction at all, and confusing them only wastes the effort.

hooks.text: **安排好的偶遇还算偶遇吗**：一旦不期而遇被写进日历、设成默认、做成产品，它跟一场准时开始的会议差在哪里？也许差别不在事先知不知道会遇上谁，而在那段时间事后要不要交账。
hooks.text_en: **Is a scheduled chance encounter still a chance encounter**: once the unplanned has been written into a calendar, set as a default and shipped as a product, what separates it from a meeting that starts on time? Perhaps the difference lies not in whether you knew who would be there, but in whether that stretch of time has to account for itself afterwards.
